summary: This DD argues that GME price movements follow predictable cycles tied to DTCC/NSCC settlement mechanics, particularly Supplementary Liquidity Deposit (SLD) cycles aligned with monthly option expirations. The author describes C+21 and C+35 calendar-day cycles as price drivers, claims SLD cycles (especially quarterly ones) are typically bullish, and explores alleged mechanisms in DTCC/NSCC systems for hiding failed-to-deliver obligations through CNS exclusions and X-REORG exemptions. It speculates that RC could execute a mandatory corporate event to trigger forced delivery of all obligations, causing a systemic squeeze.

key_claims.claim: Claims that C+21 and C+35 calendar-day cycles drive consistent, predictable GME price movements
key_claims.note: Author himself admits by page 10 (within same document) that 'C+21 used to have an effect on GME, but not anymore. It's not a decent price mover' and 'it doesn't matter how many C+ cycles you stack together at this point, even those barely move GME's price.' The framework was already failing by Aug 2021, only 7 months after the Jan 2021 spike.

key_claims.claim: Claims that SLD cycles, especially quarterly expirations, reliably produce bullish price movements and can be used to predict GME's price trajectory
key_claims.note: SLD settlement periods are real; however, the predicted consistent bullish/bearish patterns tied to SLD cycles did not reliably materialize in subsequent GME price history. The author gives SLD cycles 9/10 confidence but provides no sourced evidence for the price-movement mechanism.

key_claims.claim: Claims that Citadel or Robinhood was margin-called into crisis on Jan 28, 2021 (implied by 'a certain boy from Bulgaria got marged')
key_claims.note: SEC October 2021 report found no evidence of margin call-driven collapse. Hindsight fact: 'Citadel was never margin-called into collapse; Citadel Securities remains a major market maker.' Trading halts were driven by NSCC liquidity rules and volatility, not broker crisis.

key_claims.claim: Claims that ODS (One Day Settling Exemption) and CNS exclusions allow shorts to hide FTDs by preventing trades from appearing as fails
key_claims.note: ODS exemptions are a real SEC-regulated mechanism. However, the author explicitly warns (p. 14): 'the whole part about not appearing as a fail if you don't pass through CNS is not 100% verified. Only a person with experience in DTCC systems can 100% verify that.' The mechanics are speculative.

key_claims.claim: Claims that X-REORG exemptions in DTCC systems prevent obligations from being forced to close even if RC executes a mandatory corporate event, preventing a 'MOASS' trigger
key_claims.note: Author speculates on DTCC system mechanics without access or verification. No hindsight facts directly address X-REORG exemption behavior. However, the broader 'MOASS from corporate event' claim does not hold (see below).

key_claims.claim: Claims that RC can execute '4D Chess' via a mandatory corporate event (merger, name change, or reorganization) to force all short obligations to be closed, triggering systemic collapse ('MOASS')
key_claims.note: Written Aug 2021 predicting RC would find a way to trigger forced delivery. GameStop executed a 4-for-1 stock split (July 2022), multiple share offerings (2024-25), and added bitcoin to treasury, but no 'MOASS' or systemic event occurred. No collapse of DTCC/US financial system. Hindsight: 'No 'MOASS' ever occurred' and price remained far below thousands/millions per share predictions.

key_claims.claim: Claims that the DTCC/NSCC is operated on old, unsupported, legacy IBM systems with IT vulnerabilities and outdated protocols
key_claims.note: Author admits speculation: 'I tell they're old because i'm in IT and i know what they're talking about.' He explicitly refuses to provide sources ('Don't ask me for source. I can't give you shit'). Legacy financial infrastructure concerns have merit, but specific vulnerabilities are unsourced assertion.

key_claims.claim: Claims that DTCC/NSCC does not track or tag individual shares and there is no concept of 'float' in their system, only 'liquidity'
key_claims.note: The author correctly notes shares are not individually tagged in the DTCC system (p. 18: 'The DTCC/NSCC does not mark/tag shares'). However, this is somewhat oversimplified; the point about liquidity prioritization is valid but the presentation obscures actual DTCC operational mechanics.

validity_rationale: The book makes several falsifiable predictions that have now failed: C+21/C+35 cycles were admitted by the author himself to have lost predictive power by Aug 2021; SLD cycle patterns did not reliably drive price as predicted; RC's corporate actions (2022-2025) did not trigger a 'MOASS' or systemic event; and no collapse of DTCC/financial system occurred. The author admits the C+35 confidence as 4.5/10 and explicitly downgrades C+21 predictive value. While real market mechanics (option settlement, SLD periods, ODS rules) are mentioned, the core thesis — that these cycles predict GME price and can trigger a 'MOASS' — is undermined by both the author's own admissions and hindsight facts."
